subject: Follow-up: Data handling, retention, and subprocessor list
messages:
From: Sam Willis <sam.willis@acme-retail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Lee <security@acme-retail.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Data handling & subprocessors questions

Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the team found the latency/cost controls very compelling. A few follow-ups my security and procurement folks asked that we need answers to before we can move to a deeper security review and procurement. Quick list below: 

- Do you use customer data to train models or improve the service? 
- What is your default data retention for request/response logs and KV cache? Can retention be configured per-account?
- What logging/audit controls are available (access logs, token-level tracing, redaction options)?
- Data residency: can we restrict processing to our AWS region (us-east-1) for private/dedicated deployments or via your hosted offering?
- Subprocessors: we need a full list (telemetry vendors, analytics, cloud providers, marketplace flows). In particular, any third-party telemetry or marketplace flows that move data off our account.

Jordan (cc) is our security lead and will be on the SOC/controls review. Can you send the subprocessor list and any SOC2/attestation docs? Also please propose next steps so we can get this into our vendor review calendar.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Willis
Director of Platform Engineering
Acme Retail

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Willis <sam.willis@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Jordan Lee <security@acme-retail.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 12:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data handling & subprocessors questions

Hi Sam / Jordan — great to meet you both earlier. Below is a short recap and answers to your items, plus proposed next steps. I kept it high-level here; Rishi (cc) will join the security deep dive to cover controls and the subprocessor list in more detail.

Recap / high-level answers:
- Training: Redwood does not use customer request/response data to train or improve open models by default. We offer an opt-in program for research/aggregated telemetry that is explicitly documented and requires customer consent.
- Retention: default retention for request/response logs is 30 days; KV cache retention depends on deployment mode and can be configured per-account for Dedicated/Private (we can set to 0 days if required).
- Logging/audit: we provide request/response logs, admin access logs, and an audit trail for API key usage. Token-level tracing is available for debugging but can be disabled; PII redaction helpers are provided in SDKs and on the router.
- Data residency: for Dedicated and Private deployments we can restrict processing to your VPC/region (us-east-1). Hosted customers may be routed to our us region endpoints; we can put a routing policy on your account to prefer us-east-1.
- Subprocessors: attaching the current subprocessor inventory and our SOC 2 report (see attachments). The inventory lists cloud providers (AWS), telemetry vendors (Amplitude, Sentry for internal telemetry only, opt-outable), and our marketplace partner flow (AWS Marketplace subscription & metering — no customer content is copied to marketplace vendor accounts; billing metadata only).

Proposed next steps:
1) I can schedule a 30–45 minute security deep-dive next week with Rishi and our infra security lead to walk controls and the subprocessor inventory (suggest Wed or Thu).
2) I'll share the SOC2 and subprocessor inventory (attached) and a short FAQ doc about telemetry and marketplace flows.
3) If acceptable, we can open a HubSpot security ticket (I created one) so we capture evidence requests and timeline.

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_q2_2026.pdf (stub), SOC2_report_redwood_2025.pdf (stub)

Next steps for you: please confirm preferred time for the security call and any evidence items Jordan wants prioritized. Happy to tailor the session.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 09:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: subprocessor inventory + notes for Acme call

Marissa / Dev — putting the docs you need in one place before the call with Acme next week. Key notes to surface on the call: 

- AWS is our primary infra provider; we use customer-dedicated VPCs for Private. No customer content is shared between accounts.
- Amplitude is used for product analytics; we only send anonymized telemetry by default. For customers with strict controls we can disable Amplitude at account level.
- Sentry is only used for Redwood application errors (no customer content) and can be disabled for dedicated deployments.
- Marketplace flows (AWS Marketplace): our metering integration only sends billing/account metadata (subscription id, usage units). No PII or request/response data is transmitted to AWS Marketplace partners.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report (attached) + our data processing addendum (DPA) — I included links in the HubSpot ticket.

Drive link: https://drive.redwood.internal/shared/subprocessors_q2_2026
HubSpot ticket: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ACME-2026-EXP-17

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Lee <security@acme-retail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Sam Willis <sam.willis@acme-retail.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 08:30:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data handling & subprocessors questions

Marissa / Rishi — thanks for the quick turn on docs and the inventory. I reviewed the subprocessor list and SOC2; a couple of quick asks before we lock in the deeper review: 

- Can you confirm whether Amplitude event payloads may contain any customer PII by default? If so, what fields are redacted?
- For Hosted routing: please confirm the hostname/endpoint that would be used if we request a us-east-1 routing policy. We want to validate through our network team.
- For Marketplace flows: please provide a short diagram or paragraph that explicitly states what metadata is sent to AWS Marketplace and how it's scoped to billing only.

We'll aim for the Wed 06/17 10:00am PT slot for the security deep-dive. I can invite procurement for the billing/marketplace piece if needed.

Thanks,
Jordan Lee
Security Lead, Acme Retail
security@acme-retail.com
